_what_this_is: The fleet's only authority on hostname -> node_id. Specified in docs/node-identity-protocol.md (adoption step 4). Its job is twofold: stop a node from naming itself something that collides, and let the console resolve a hostname it sees on a row into a node it knows.
_lookup_rules: Lookups are CASE-INSENSITIVE. One machine reports itself three ways: $env:COMPUTERNAME uppercase, hostname.exe and DNS in mixed case, and the device bridge lowercase. All three were observed on ZOLTARGENESIS in a single session on 2026-09-07.
Resolve against `map` first. If there is no hit, try `former_names` — a historical row written before a rename still has to resolve to the node that wrote it.
A value of null means the hostname is NOT KNOWN, not that the node does not exist. Render it as a gap, never as unresolved-therefore-absent.

_schema_note: docs/node-identity-protocol.md sketches this file as a flat hostname->node_id object. That shape cannot express a former name, an explicit unknown, or where a value came from — all three of which were needed on day one. The flat map is preserved under `map` so the sketched lookup still works; the rest is additive. If the protocol is ratified in its original shape, `map` alone is the file.
